title: What an owner's browser loads in the admin
headline: The admin's browser load is moderately bloated, and the worst of it is cheap to fix before opening: a plain screen loads 1.15 MB of script (median of 449 routes), of which 481 KB is Supabase's client, zod and the builder's English, brought in by three stray imports. 26 screens load an editor they never draw, an order screen carries 0.69 MB for custom fields the store may not have, one Work screen ships a 1.7 MB chunk of text, and the builder loads 3.3 MB at once. Four small fixes (AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-7) and two checks (AC-10, AC-11) take a plain screen to about 0.72 MB and keep the leaks from coming back; the builder, the text handed down in each page (36 to 85% of its data) and link prefetching (23 to 46 background requests a screen) need more care. Two things the report missed are added: the notice badge costs four database statements per open tab per minute whatever the store uses (AC-13), and the Products list sends every product to the browser at about 0.9 KB each (AC-14, already code review step 1.13, open); no finding judges a feature by its use, and every cost is per screen view, so it starts the day owners arrive.

findings.title: Three stray imports put Supabase, zod and the builder's English on every admin screen
findings.evidence: Chunks in the first load of 420 to 432 of 449 admin routes, each opened: supabase-js 179,419 bytes (44,575 gzip), Supabase realtime 57,349, a Buffer polyfill module 22,701, zod 116,870 (32,996 gzip), the builder's English 71,508, schemas built on zod 33,198. The only paths from the signed-in layout, by my import graph: session.tsx to lib/supabase/client.ts to env.ts (zod); push-settings.tsx, which holds the 9-line AdminServiceWorker, to lib/push.ts (zod); shortcut-sheet.tsx to responsive-edit.tsx for the 4-line typingIn(), and responsive-edit imports builder.en and the responsive schemas. With those three edges cut, the store home's client closure falls from 100 files (705,818 bytes of source) to 87 (432,239) and reaches none of zod, @supabase or builder.en. The verified report counted what still needs them after the cut: zod 160 routes, Supabase 83, builder.en 40.
findings.cost: 481 KB raw / about 137 KB gzip in the first load of every signed-in admin screen, 43% of the 1.12 MB all screens share. Downloaded once per browser until a deploy changes a chunk (the builder's English changes whenever a builder word does); parsed and run on every full page load.
findings.who_pays: An owner's browser on every full load of any admin screen, phones most. The team today; every owner and staff member once the platform opens.

findings.title: The notice badge asks the server every minute from every open admin tab: four database statements a time, one of them thrown away
findings.evidence: useNoticeCount() asks /admin/account/notices/feed?place=...&count=1 when the admin opens, every NOTICE_POLL_MS (60,000) while the tab is visible, and when the tab is shown again. It runs in the AI manager's launcher, which is in the store's and the platform's layout, so every screen of a signed-in owner has it. The browser run shows it on all 13 store screens sampled: one GET after load, 1,731 bytes on the wire for a 12-byte answer. What one answer costs, read from the route: getAccount() verifies the token and selects the account (auth.ts line 138), and for a session without a second step calls Supabase Auth once (getUser, line 148); placeOf() selects the store by its slug (route.ts line 22); then listNotices(account.id, place, 1) (line 32) selects the newest notice joined to its store, whose rows the count answer does not use, and unreadNotices() counts. Four statements, one discarded, and up to one Auth round trip. Notices are written only by the AI manager's background work (page builds, follow-ups, plans, approvals, reports, hand-offs).
findings.cost: Per visible admin tab: 60 requests and 240 statements an hour, whether or not the AI manager has ever left that person a notice. Arithmetic, not a measurement: 1,000 owners with the admin visible are 1,000 function calls and 4,000 statements a minute.
findings.who_pays: The server per request and the database, and Supabase Auth for sessions without a second step; the owner's browser a little. It grows with the number of open admin tabs, not with use of notices.
